forecast-period.text: A ridge of high pressure lies over eastern parts of SA, while a low pressure system in WA extends a trough into the west. The low and trough will move across the state on Friday, clearing to the east by Saturday morning as a brief high pressure system settles over SA. Another low is expected to enter from the west on Sunday, moving over central and eastern parts on Monday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers and possible thunderstorms moving across the state, clearing from the west during the day, reaching eastern districts during the evening. Storms more likely through western and central parts. Maximum temperatures near to above average. Fresh north to northeasterly winds, tending west to southwesterly from the west during the day.

Showers and thunderstorms in the west and north, possibly severe in the west with risks of destructive wind gusts, giant hail and heavy rainfall during the afternoon and evening. East to northeasterly winds, tending northerly and becoming fresh at times in the west.

Possible thunderstorms about the southeast during the morning. Showers about the agricultural areas, contracting to the southeast during the day. Maximum temperatures near to above average. Light winds in the west, tending northeasterly during the day. Elsewhere, west to southwesterly winds, fresh at times near the eastern boarder, easing late.

Showers and possible thunderstorms about southern and central areas, clearing from the West Coast by the evening. Maximum temperatures above average in the west, grading to below average in the southeast. Light and variable winds about the eastern border. Elsewhere, north to northeasterly winds, fresh about the North West Pastoral district, easing from the west and tending southwesterly late.

text.p: Showers and possible thunderstorms about central and southeastern parts. Maximum temperatures near to above average. North to northeasterly winds about the east at first, tending south to southwesterly about the west and extending throughout during the day.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Monday: Less than 2 mm across the far northeast. Elsewhere, broadly 2 to 10 mm increasing to 10 to 20 mm across the west and the Southern Agricultural Area, with thunderstorms possibly producing isolated falls up to 40 mm.
